keyVerseText: And a mixed multitude went up also with them; and flocks, and herds, even very much cattle. a mixed: Heb. a great mixture
rootMeaning: The root word עָרַב (ʻârab) conveys the idea of mingling, intermixing, or engaging in exchange, such as pledging or undertaking. This root sense emphasizes a coming together or intertwining, which extends metaphorically to the noun עֵרֶב (ʻêreb) as something mixed or interwoven. Beyond the common English gloss of 'mixture' or 'woof,' the root highlights a dynamic interaction or binding together, whether of people, threads, or agreements.
usageInScripture: The word עֵרֶב appears 13 times in Scripture, primarily translated as 'woof' or 'in the woof,' referring to the transverse threads in weaving that interlace with the warp. It also denotes a mixed multitude or mingled group, as seen in Exodus 12:38. This range—from a literal weaving term to describing a heterogeneous assembly—reveals how the concept of interwoven or mingled elements underlies its usage, whether in physical fabric or social composition.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding עֵרֶב in its original sense enriches our grasp of biblical imagery and community. The notion of mingling or interweaving reflects how God’s people are composed of diverse elements brought together under His sovereign design. It reminds believers that unity in the body of Christ involves the blending of distinct individuals into a harmonious whole. This word also points to God's providential inclusion of outsiders, illustrating His grace in forming a covenant community that transcends ethnic or social boundaries, foreshadowing the gospel's call to all nations.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 12:38 speaks of 'a mixed multitude' going up with the Israelites, emphasizing a diverse group accompanying God's chosen people. The term עֵרֶב here conveys more than mere numbers; it highlights the mingling of different peoples united in the Exodus event. This underscores God’s redemptive reach beyond Israel alone, inviting reflection on how His salvation includes those who come from various backgrounds to join His covenant community.
